actions.action: Raised donor funds and distributed USD 5.926m in 2024 cash grants to eight foreign ELNET entities, including USD 1.034m to ELNET France.
Used grant programs described as educating European leaders through seminars, debates, colloquia, Israel visits/study trips and digital exchange.
Conducted declared French interest-representation activities targeting laws, public decisions, government and parliament with EUR 100k-200k annual declared lobbying expenditure.
Issued a EUR 72,000 sole-supplier engagement to ELNET Europe-Israel for an event at the French Senate on 10 November 2025.

axes.question: What upstream grants to Friends of ELNET are general versus program-restricted?
How much did Friends of ELNET transfer to each foreign ELNET entity and for what program purpose?
Can the ELNET France foreign grant be allocated to declared French lobbying expenditure and named influence actions?
Is there a specific Israeli-state funding/tasking edge to an ELNET entity tied to a French institutional event?

causal.causal_right: US tax filings directly document donor grants to the US hub and Schedule F cash grants to named foreign affiliates.
causal.counter: Many donor grants are general support; donor intent/tasking does not automatically propagate downstream.
causal.limit: Closes resource-flow topology, not downstream political causality.
causal.mechanism: private foundations/donors -> Friends of ELNET US -> foreign ELNET affiliates

causal.causal_right: The US grant to ELNET France and the existence of a substantial declared French lobbying operation are both established; Schedule O describes leader-education/trip/event purposes overlapping with advocacy capacity.
causal.counter: No inspected allocation ledger maps the USD 1.034m grant to the EUR 100k-200k HATVP lobbying category or to a named action.
causal.gap: Need restricted-fund terms, French accounts and project-level cost allocation to attribute Friends of ELNET grant dollars to named ELNET France lobbying actions.
causal.limit: Resource/capacity link is plausible and partially supported; action-level funding attribution remains open.
causal.mechanism: Friends of ELNET US grant -> ELNET France resources/program capacity -> French lobbying operation

causal.causal_right: The official procurement notice names the ministry, supplier, amount, sole-supplier basis and one-day engagement tied to the French Senate event.
causal.counter: The notice does not establish control over ELNET France generally or causal effect on a French decision.
causal.mechanism: Israeli MFA -> EUR 72k sole-supplier procurement -> ELNET Europe-Israel -> French Senate event

causal.causal_right: Funding and lobbying actions exist in the same organizational ecosystem, but the public corpus lacks the intermediate allocation/tasking records and counterfactual outcome design.
causal.counter: HATVP records French actions as own-account; some upstream grants are general support; France-level lobbying spend is a narrower accounting category than total grant receipts.
causal.gap: Grant agreements/ledgers/instructions and policy-footprint evidence required.
causal.limit: Cannot promote funding to command, capture or policy causation.
causal.mechanism: foreign/private funding -> tasking of ELNET France -> named lobbying action -> French policy outcome

claims.claim: Friends of ELNET functions as a US fundraising/grantmaking hub that transferred USD 5.926 million in 2024 to eight foreign ELNET entities.
claims.counter: The filing establishes transfers and stated program purpose, not control over every downstream action.

claims.claim: ELNET France received USD 1,034,210 from Friends of ELNET in 2024.
claims.counter: The public Schedule F does not break this grant into French lobbying versus other programs, trips, events or overhead.

claims.claim: Friends of ELNET foreign grants are explicitly described as supporting European-leader education, seminars/debates/colloquia, Israel visits/study trips and digital exchange.
claims.counter: A broad program-purpose statement does not identify which affiliate dollar financed which named event or policy intervention.

claims.claim: ELNET France has a declared French lobbying operation with EUR 100k-200k annual interest-representation expenditure and 3 FTE in 2023-2025, and declares activity for its own account.
claims.counter: Own-account registration under HATVP does not establish that no foreign grants support the organization; conversely foreign funding does not make every activity foreign-tasked.

claims.claim: The public corpus does not establish a dollar/euro-level allocation from the USD 1.034m Friends of ELNET grant to named HATVP lobbying actions, nor donor tasking of a specific French policy position.
claims.counter: The broad grant purpose overlaps with some influence activities, so absence of allocation data is not proof of functional separation.
claims.gap: Need ELNET France accounts, grant agreement/budget, restricted-fund ledger or project-level expenditure mapping to connect foreign grant dollars to named HATVP actions.

claims.claim: At least one upstream private-foundation grant to Friends of ELNET carried an explicit program restriction tied to the Brussels office and high-level Israel-delegation programming.
claims.counter: This 2019 William Davidson Foundation grant does not prove restrictions on all donors or downstream French policy tasking.

claims.claim: The Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs directly funded a specific ELNET Europe-Israel operation connected to a French Senate event through a EUR 72,000 sole-supplier procurement.
claims.counter: A specific public procurement closes state funding/tasking for that project only; it does not establish general Israeli-state command of ELNET France or the network.

controls.control: HATVP records ELNET France interest-representation activities as undertaken for its own account; this blocks automatic reclassification as acting for a foreign client.
HATVP lobbying expenditure is a bounded regulatory category and cannot be directly compared with total organizational grants as if they measured the same thing.
Friends of ELNET reports no US lobbying under the IRS Form 990 lobbying question; this is jurisdiction/category-specific and does not negate French affiliate lobbying.
William Davidson Foundation evidence shows at least one program-restricted upstream grant, but a single restricted donor cannot be generalized to all funders.
Israeli MFA procurement proves a specific state-funded task but cannot be extrapolated into general state command of ELNET France/network.
Large foreign grant receipts plus French policy advocacy do not establish downstream policy effect without an allocation/tasking and decision-footprint chain.

facts.subject: ELNET France HATVP representation status
facts.value: ELNET France is registered as an interest representative; its 2025 activity sheets state that the represented interest is ELNET France itself (en propre).

facts.subject: ELNET France declared lobbying expenditure 2025
facts.value: For 2025 ELNET France declared between EUR 100,000 and EUR 200,000 of expenditure devoted to interest-representation actions and 3 FTE staff; the same expenditure bracket and 3 FTE are shown for 2023 and 2024.

facts.subject: ELNET France declared policy-influence methods
facts.value: A 2025 ELNET France activity sheet on strengthening legislation/regulation against Islamism declares methods including transmitting suggestions to influence drafting of a public decision, online influence strategies, correspondence, events and meetings.

facts.subject: HATVP lobbying resource perimeter
facts.value: HATVP rules define declared interest-representation resources as a bounded category of means devoted to lobbying activities; this category is not the same as an organization’s total operating budget or all program expenditure.

facts.subject: Friends of ELNET 2024 revenue and contributions
facts.value: Friends of ELNET reported USD 8,955,347 total revenue in 2024, including USD 8,679,742 in contributions and grants.

facts.subject: Friends of ELNET 2024 foreign grants total
facts.value: Friends of ELNET reported USD 5,926,477 in grants and similar amounts paid; Schedule F lists eight foreign ELNET recipient entities whose cash grants sum exactly to USD 5,926,477.

facts.subject: Friends of ELNET grant to ELNET France
facts.value: Schedule F lists a USD 1,034,210 electronic cash grant to ELNET, France in 2024.

facts.subject: Friends of ELNET 2024 affiliate grant distribution
facts.value: Schedule F lists 2024 grants to ELNET Brussels USD 685,202; France USD 1,034,210; Germany USD 904,528; Global USD 929,486; Israel USD 880,438; Italy USD 415,522; Poland USD 496,500; UK USD 580,591.

facts.subject: Friends of ELNET stated foreign-grant program purpose
facts.value: Schedule O states that foreign grants support education of European leaders, seminars, public debates, newsletters, lectures and colloquia, visits and study trips to Israel, and internet/new-technology exchange of ideas.

facts.subject: Friends of ELNET 2024 program service expense
facts.value: Friends of ELNET reported USD 7,029,701 in program-service expenses in 2024, including USD 5,926,477 of grants.

facts.subject: Friends of ELNET US lobbying checkbox
facts.value: On its 2024 US Form 990, Friends of ELNET answered No to the IRS question asking whether the US 501(c)(3) engaged in lobbying activities; this is a US tax-form classification and does not classify foreign affiliates under French law.

facts.subject: Friends of ELNET FY2025 growth
facts.value: ProPublica’s IRS-derived data for FY2025 reports USD 10,705,776 revenue and USD 10,307,022 contributions, showing continued large-scale donor financing after 2024.

facts.subject: Israeli MFA ELNET Europe-Israel procurement amount
facts.value: Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs exemption notice 4000606739 records a EUR 72,000 sole-supplier engagement with ELNET Europe-Israel.

facts.subject: Israeli MFA ELNET procurement French Senate event
facts.value: The procurement notice concerns an ELNET Europe event at the French Senate, with engagement start and end on 10 November 2025; the supplier tax number is 580535672.

facts.subject: William Davidson Foundation restricted-purpose grant to Friends of ELNET
facts.value: The William Davidson Foundation 2019 Form 990-PF specifies a Friends of ELNET grant purpose: support the Brussels office and creation of high-level programming for Israel delegations.

facts.subject: ELNET France 2025 declared policy objectives
facts.value: ELNET France declared 2025 objectives including opposing French recognition of a Palestinian state, strengthening legislation/regulation on Islamism and anti-Jewish hatred, and strengthening France-Europe-Israel/Abraham Accords diplomatic relations.
